REQ_001.polished: The clinic has one main site and one remote branch, a limited budget, and expects to grow from 30 to 80 staff within two years. Business goals: keep patient care running with minimal downtime, allow both sites to share patient records, and support growth to 80 staff without a redesign. Technical goals: reliable internet at both sites, using a primary ISP and a lower-cost backup link; a site-to-site VPN between the main site and the branch; and network segmentation that separates clinical traffic from administrative and guest traffic. Constraints: the limited budget favours affordable business-grade equipment, the IT team is small or outsourced, and the branch operates only on weekdays. Growth: switches and the IP addressing plan are sized for 80 users from the start. Security: patient records are encrypted in transit through the VPN and at rest, each site has a firewall, accounts use MFA, and access is granted by role.

LOG_001.polished: I would use a three-layer hierarchical design: access switches for user connections, a distribution layer that routes between departments and enforces policy, and a fast switching core. For segmentation, HR, Finance and Engineering each receive their own VLAN, the Engineering lab has a separate VLAN to isolate its traffic, and a management VLAN serves network devices. The addressing plan allocates one private subnet per VLAN, for example HR 10.10.10.0/24, Finance 10.20.20.0/24, Engineering 10.30.30.0/23 for its larger device count, the lab 10.40.40.0/24 and management 10.99.0.0/24. For routing, inter-VLAN routing runs on layer 3 switches at the distribution layer, with ACLs that restrict Finance to the traffic it needs and stop the lab reaching other departments. For redundancy, two distribution switches share the default gateway through HSRP or VRRP, each access switch has dual uplinks, and core links use link aggregation.
LOG_001.rough: I will use hierarchical design of 3 layer: access switches where users connect, distribution layer it route between departments and apply the policy, and core is fast switching. For segmentation HR, Finance and Engineering each one take own VLAN, Engineering lab have separate VLAN for isolate the traffic, and management VLAN for devices. Addressing plan give one private subnet each VLAN, example HR 10.10.10.0/24, Finance 10.20.20.0/24, Engineering 10.30.30.0/23 because more devices, lab 10.40.40.0/24 and management 10.99.0.0/24. For routing, inter VLAN routing is on layer 3 switches in distribution, with ACLs so Finance only get the traffic it need and lab cannot reach other departments. For redundancy two distribution switches share default gateway by HSRP or VRRP, every access switch have dual uplinks, and core links use link aggregation.

PROT_001.polished: I would choose OSPF for a multi-building campus that will grow. As a link-state protocol, every router holds a full map of the network and calculates its own best paths, so it converges quickly after a link failure compared with distance-vector protocols such as RIP. It scales by dividing the campus into areas, with area 0 as the backbone and an area per building or group of buildings, so routing updates stay inside each area and a new building is simply a new area. It is also an open standard, which keeps the campus free to mix vendors over time.
PROT_001.rough: I choose OSPF for campus with many buildings that will grow. It is link state protocol, so all router have full map of network and calculate the best path by itself, so it converge fast after link fail compare to distance vector like RIP. It scale by divide campus in areas, area 0 is backbone and one area for each building or group of buildings, so routing updates stay inside the area and new building is only new area. Also it is open standard, so campus can mix different vendors in future.

SEC_001.polished: For perimeter security, a firewall sits between the internet and the company network to block unwanted inbound traffic, and remote employees connect through a VPN so their sessions to internal applications are encrypted. The public website uses HTTPS. Staff use strong passwords and receive training to recognise phishing emails.

Public website use HTTPS. Staffs use strong password and take training to know the phishing emails.
